text:
Easton Cowan has gone from a prospect the Leafs were patient with to a player they're building lines around. After 29 points in 66 games as a rookie, he has 14 in 17 this season, and on Nov. 2 TSN reported he was back beside Auston Matthews after a rocky end to a road trip. At the same time, a Yardbarker rumor piece says any Maple Leafs blockbuster may have to include him, which is its own kind of compliment.

How much is real? Toronto's expected-goal share is almost 11 points better with Cowan on at five on five than without him, the strongest sign in his profile. The finishing is the warm part: he's about two goals ahead of his chances, and the Leafs have scored four more than expected with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (a small, nine-game sample) had him carrying the puck in and setting up shots at a 94th-percentile rate. Among forwards picked around 28th overall, the median first full season is 0.35 points a game. He's well past that.
headline: From patient prospect to Matthews' wing
